gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Zowietek ZowieREC 4K records only 1080p60 when its source sends 4K60 or 1080p120 (it can still pass that signal through), so a PS5 or Xbox at its 4K60 default gets 1080p files, while the ClonerAlliance UHD Pro records 4K30 from the same source.
standout_why: I compared against the cited pages: the ClonerAlliance UHD Pro product page and knowledgebase, the RecDual Dongle page, the AVerMedia EzRecorder 330 product page (rs locale, cited in chat 3), the EzRecorder 330 datasheet and the Hauppauge HD PVR Pro 60 listing on streameez. None of ChatGPT's results came from zowietek.com. ChatGPT's own ZowieREC card in chat 2 said 'Records up to 4K30 ... Supports 4K60 passthrough', which suggests 4K recording from a 4K60 console. Several facts in my angle are already on cited pages and are not new: the UHD Pro's 8 TB HDD and GPT/MBR support, its Smart TV exclusion and its 4K60-to-4K30 recording; the RecDual's lack of HDR and its need for DP Alt Mode; and the ER330's 2 TB partition rule, missing USB flash support and lack of HDCP support.
decides: For console players (PS5 or Xbox at 4K60) who want 4K files, this moves the pick from the $199 ZowieREC 4K to the ClonerAlliance UHD Pro or UHD Pro Max. The ZowieREC only gives 4K30 files when the source itself outputs 4K30. If 1080p60 is enough, the ZowieREC and the EzRecorder 330 stay valid. Note that the EzRecorder 330 cannot use USB flash drives and needs drives over 2 TB partitioned to 2 TB.

findings.label: Recording from a 4K60 or 1080p120 source
findings.value: Accepts 4K60 and 1080p120 input and loops it out at 4K60 or 1080p120. Recording and streaming are downgraded to 1080p60.
findings.source_title: Can it record 4K60 or 1080P120? – Zowietek knowledge base
findings.note: Quoted from the article body: 'Yes, it supports 4K60 and 1080P120 input, with loop-out at 4K60 or 1080P120,' ... 'recording and streaming are downgraded to 1080P60.' The article has no date.

findings.label: 4K loop-out by source rate
findings.value: A 4K60 input loops out at 4K60; a 4K30 input loops out at 4K30
findings.source_title: 4k hdmi video recorder – Zowietek knowledge base category
findings.note: From the 'Can HDMI output 4k?' entry as shown on the category page.

findings.label: HDCP sources
findings.value: Not supported. With an HDCP source the Dashboard shows 'Check HDMI Setting'.
findings.source_title: Does it support HDCP? – Zowietek knowledge base
findings.note: Quoted: 'ZowieREC does not support HDCP.' The Zowietek PS5 connection guide for the encoder line says to turn HDCP off in the console's system settings.

findings.label: HDMI input version and cables
findings.value: HDMI 2.0 input. HDMI 2.1 or 8K cables work only if they are backward compatible with 2.0.
findings.source_title: 4k hdmi video recorder – Zowietek knowledge base category
findings.note: From the 'Does it support 2.1 or 8k hdmi cables?' entry as shown on the category page.

findings.label: Excluded sources and playback
findings.value: Cannot record Smart TV apps directly; a separate HDMI source device is needed. Plays back only files the recorder itself made.
findings.source_title: 4k hdmi video recorder – Zowietek knowledge base category
findings.note: From the 'Can I record videos directly from a Smart TV?' and Dish Network external-drive playback entries.

findings.product: Zowietek ZowieBox (same NAS stack, 'Zowietek series products')
findings.label: NAS protocol
findings.value: CIFS only, no NFS; SMB 1.0, 2.0 and 3.0 (3.0 is the default, changed with vers= in the mount options)
findings.source_title: How to use NAS to save video file – Zowietek knowledge base
findings.note: The guide is written for the ZowieBox and says 'Zowietek series products support SMB1.0, SMB2.0 and SMB3.0'. It does not name the ZowieREC.

findings.label: Storage limits and file systems
findings.value: USB flash drives up to 512 GB, external HDD up to 8 TB, microSD; exFAT, NTFS or FAT/FAT32; GPT and MBR
findings.source_title: ClonerAlliance UHD Pro - Standalone 4K H.265/H.264 HDMI Video & Gaming Recorder
findings.note: Already on a cited rival page. The page gives no microSD capacity limit.

findings.label: 4K60 source and source exclusions
findings.value: A 4K60 source records at up to 4K30 with 4K60 passthrough; 4K60 capture works only over the USB-C 3.0 UVC link to a PC. 'Smart TVs and TV Antennas are NOT supported as input video sources.' Mini or Micro HDMI sources need a Type-A adapter (not included).
findings.source_title: ClonerAlliance UHD Pro - Standalone 4K H.265/H.264 HDMI Video & Gaming Recorder
findings.note: Already on a cited rival page. The page has no HDCP or HDR statement.

findings.label: Storage compatibility
findings.value: microSD up to 512 GB; USB flash drives not supported; USB HDD or SSD over 2 TB must be split into partitions of 2 TB or less; NAS over 4 TB must be split into partitions of 4 TB or less
findings.note: Quoted: 'EzRecorder 330 does not support USB flash drives.' and 'For drives larger than 2TB, please create a partition of 2TB or less before use.' This page was cited in chat 3, so the fact is not new. The page names no NAS protocol.

findings.label: Inputs, passthrough and HDCP
findings.value: Accepts 2160p, 1080p, 1080i, 720p, 576p, 576i, 480p and 480i; passes through up to 4Kp60; records up to 1080p60 in H.264 or H.265 with AAC; does not record HDCP-protected signals
findings.note: Quoted: 'ER330 does not support viewing/recording/streaming of HDCP protected signals'.

findings.label: HDR, USB-C input and HDCP
findings.value: No HDR content (turn HDR off on the source); the USB-C DP input needs DisplayPort Alt Mode on the source; HDCP sources are not supported; files are FAT32, exFAT or NTFS
findings.source_title: ClonerAlliance RecDual Dongle - Portable HDMI & USB-C Video Recorder
findings.note: Already on a cited rival page. Records 1080p60 H.264 with 4K60 passthrough.

findings.label: Accepted formats and media
findings.value: SD (NTSC, PAL), 720p50 and 720p59.94, 1080p23.98 to 1080p60. The 2160p standards are tied to the 4K Pro model. Records H.264, ProRes or DNxHD to SD or UHS-II cards or USB disks formatted ExFAT or HFS+. 12 V DC power, supply included. US$575.
findings.source_title: HyperDeck Shuttle – Tech Specs | Blackmagic Design
findings.note: The ExFAT and HFS+ wording covers the whole HyperDeck Shuttle line. The page has no HDCP statement. MSRP includes duties but excludes sales tax and shipping.
